papers.title: An Accurate and Efficient Approach to Knowledge Extraction from Scientific Publications Using Structured Ontology Models, Graph Neural Networks, and Large Language Models
papers.abstract: The rapid growth of biomedical literature makes it challenging for researchers to stay current. Integrating knowledge from various sources is crucial for studying complex biological systems. Traditional text-mining methods often have limited accuracy because they don’t capture semantic and contextual nuances. Deep-learning models can be computationally expensive and typically have low interpretability, though efforts in explainable AI aim to mitigate this. Furthermore, transformer-based models have a tendency to produce false or made-up information—a problem known as hallucination—which is especially prevalent in large language models (LLMs). This study proposes a hybrid approach combining text-mining techniques with graph neural networks (GNNs) and fine-tuned large language models (LLMs) to extend biomedical knowledge graphs and interpret predicted edges based on published literature. An LLM is used to validate predictions and provide explanations. Evaluated on a corpus of experimentally confirmed protein interactions, the approach achieved a Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC) of 0.772. Applied to insomnia, the approach identified 25 interactions between 32 human proteins absent in known knowledge bases, including regulatory interactions between MAOA and 5-HT2C, binding between ADAM22 and 14-3-3 proteins, which is implicated in neurological diseases, and a circadian regulatory loop involving RORB and NR1D1. The hybrid GNN-LLM method analyzes biomedical literature efficiency to uncover potential molecular interactions for complex disorders. It can accelerate therapeutic target discovery by focusing expert verification on the most relevant automatically extracted information.

papers.title: AI Agent-Driven Framework for Automated Product Knowledge Graph Construction in E-Commerce
papers.abstract: The rapid expansion of e-commerce platforms generates vast amounts of unstructured product data, creating significant challenges for information retrieval, recommendation systems, and data analytics. Knowledge Graphs (KGs) offer a structured, interpretable format to organize such data, yet constructing product-specific KGs remains a complex and manual process. This paper introduces a fully automated, AI agent-driven framework for constructing product knowledge graphs directly from unstructured product descriptions. Leveraging Large Language Models (LLMs), our method operates in three stages using dedicated agents: ontology creation and expansion, ontology refinement, and knowledge graph population. This agent-based approach ensures semantic coherence, scalability, and high-quality output without relying on predefined schemas or handcrafted extraction rules. We evaluate the system on a real-world dataset of air conditioner product descriptions, demonstrating strong performance in both ontology generation and KG population. The framework achieves over 97\% property coverage and minimal redundancy, validating its effectiveness and practical applicability. Our work highlights the potential of LLMs to automate structured knowledge extraction in retail, providing a scalable path toward intelligent product data integration and utilization.

papers.title: Hierarchical Attentional Hybrid Neural Networks for Document Classification
papers.abstract: Document classification is a challenging task with important applications. The deep learning approaches to the problem have gained much attention recently. Despite the progress, the proposed models do not incorporate the knowledge of the document structure in the architecture efficiently and not take into account the contexting importance of words and sentences. In this paper, we propose a new approach based on a combination of convolutional neural networks, gated recurrent units, and attention mechanisms for document classification tasks. The main contribution of this work is the use of convolution layers to extract more meaningful, generalizable and abstract features by the hierarchical representation. The proposed method in this paper improves the results of the current attention-based approaches for document classification.

papers.title: Combining machine learning, simulations and experiments for improved glass design
papers.abstract: The design of novel glasses with tailored properties remains a grand challenge in materials science, traditionally requiring extensive trial-and-error experimentation. This talk presents a comprehensive framework that integrates machine learning, atomistic simulations, and targeted experiments to accelerate the discovery and optimization of glass compositions. We demonstrate how large-scale machine learning models trained on experimental databases can predict glass properties across nearly the entire periodic table, enabling rapid screening of promising compositions. These predictions are refined through physics-informed graph neural networks that capture atomic-scale interactions and energy conservation principles, providing deeper insights into structure-property relationships. The framework is enhanced by automated knowledge extraction from scientific literature using our materials-specific language model (MatSciBERT) and natural language processing techniques. We showcase practical applications including the development of radiation-resistant nuclear waste glasses, scratch-resistant display glasses, and specialty glasses for space applications. The talk concludes by highlighting how this integrated approach has led to the discovery of novel glass compositions with superior properties, validated through experimental synthesis and characterization. Our results demonstrate that the synergistic combination of artificial intelligence, computational modeling, and experimental validation can significantly accelerate the glass design process while reducing resource requirements and environmental impact.

papers.title: The Deep Arbitrary Polynomial Chaos Neural Network or how Deep Artificial Neural Networks could benefit from Data-Driven Homogeneous Chaos Theory
papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence and Machine learning have been widely used in various fields of mathematical computing, physical modeling, computational science, communication science, and stochastic analysis. Approaches based on Deep Artificial Neural Networks (DANN) are very popular in our days. Depending on the learning task, the exact form of DANNs is determined via their multi-layer architecture, activation functions and the so-called loss function. However, for a majority of deep learning approaches based on DANNs, the kernel structure of neural signal processing remains the same, where the node response is encoded as a linear superposition of neural activity, while the non-linearity is triggered by the activation functions. In the current paper, we suggest to analyze the neural signal processing in DANNs from the point of view of homogeneous chaos theory as known from polynomial chaos expansion (PCE). From the PCE perspective, the (linear) response on each node of a DANN could be seen as a $1^{st}$ degree multi-variate polynomial of single neurons from the previous layer, i.e. linear weighted sum of monomials. From this point of view, the conventional DANN structure relies implicitly (but erroneously) on a Gaussian distribution of neural signals. Additionally, this view revels that by design DANNs do not necessarily fulfill any orthogonality or orthonormality condition for a majority of data-driven applications. Therefore, the prevailing handling of neural signals in DANNs could lead to redundant representation as any neural signal could contain some partial information from other neural signals. To tackle that challenge, we suggest to employ the data-driven generalization of PCE theory known as arbitrary polynomial chaos (aPC) to construct a corresponding multi-variate orthonormal representations on each node of a DANN to obtain Deep arbitrary polynomial chaos neural networks.

summary: The literature on Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) for knowledge discovery highlights advancements in knowledge extraction techniques, particularly through the integration of GNNs and Large Language Models (LLMs) to manage unstructured data in various domains. However, significant gaps remain in empirical validation, interpretability, and the application of these methods beyond specific fields like biomedical literature and e-commerce. Additionally, the exploration of chaos theory in deep learning presents a novel perspective that could enhance GNN architectures, yet lacks practical applications and empirical support. Overall, the research underscores the need for further investigation into the scalability and effectiveness of GNNs in diverse scientific contexts.
scholarly_positioning: Existing research on Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) for knowledge extraction has predominantly focused on specific domains, such as biomedical literature, leaving a gap in empirical validation and broader applicability across scientific fields. While advancements in integrating GNNs with Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown promise, challenges such as model interpretability and the risk of hallucination remain unresolved. Moreover, the theoretical exploration of chaos theory in deep learning lacks practical applications, highlighting a disconnect between innovative frameworks and their empirical validation. This proposed research aims to bridge these gaps by developing a comprehensive GNN framework for large-scale knowledge discovery in scientific literature, addressing the limitations of existing methodologies and contributing to a more robust understanding of knowledge extraction processes across diverse domains.
research_scope: This empirical study will focus on the application of Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) integrated with Large Language Models (LLMs) for knowledge extraction from scientific literature across multiple domains, including biomedical and e-commerce. The evaluation period will span six months, during which the model's performance will be assessed against traditional machine learning models and existing GNN frameworks. Primary outcomes will include accuracy, F1 score, and Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC) in knowledge extraction tasks, while secondary outcomes will focus on model interpretability scores. The study will utilize fixed dataset splits from diverse scientific literature databases to ensure robust comparisons and control for potential overfitting. By addressing the limitations of existing methodologies, this research aims to enhance the scalability and effectiveness of GNNs in knowledge discovery, contributing to a deeper understanding of knowledge extraction processes.
concept_definition:
{
  "Graph Neural Networks (GNNs)": "A type of neural network designed to process data structured as graphs, capturing relationships and dependencies between nodes (entities) effectively.",
  "Large Language Models (LLMs)": "Advanced neural networks trained on vast text corpora to understand and generate human-like text, capable of contextual comprehension and language generation.",
  "Knowledge Extraction": "The process of identifying and extracting structured information from unstructured text, such as scientific literature, to facilitate data analysis and discovery.",
  "Accuracy": "A metric representing the proportion of true positive and true negative predictions made by the model out of all predictions.",
  "F1 Score": "A measure of a model's accuracy that considers both precision and recall, providing a balance between the two in knowledge extraction tasks.",
  "Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC)": "A metric that provides a balanced measure of the quality of binary classifications, taking into account true and false positives and negatives.",
  "Model Interpretability": "The degree to which a human can understand the cause of a decision made by a machine learning model, often assessed through various methods.",
  "Probing": "An interpretability method that analyzes the internal representations of a model to understand how specific features contribute to predictions.",
  "Attribution": "A technique that assigns importance scores to input features based on their contribution to the model's output, helping to explain decisions.",
  "Attention Visualization": "A method that visualizes the attention weights of a model, indicating which parts of the input the model focuses on when making predictions.",
  "Activation Steering": "An interpretability technique that manipulates the internal activations of a model to observe changes in output, revealing decision pathways.",
  "Safety Monitor": "A system that evaluates the outputs of a model for safety concerns, ensuring that generated responses do not pose risks to users.",
  "Explanation Generation": "The process of creating human-readable explanations for model predictions, aimed at enhancing user understanding and trust.",
  "User Trust": {
    "Trust Calibration": "The alignment of a user's confidence in a model's predictions with the actual accuracy of those predictions.",
    "Blind Trust": "A scenario where users rely on a model without understanding its workings or limitations.",
    "Perceived Transparency": "The degree to which users feel that they understand how a model operates and makes decisions.",
    "Appropriate Reliance": "The extent to which users depend on a model's predictions based on its demonstrated reliability and interpretability."
  },
  "Safety Outcomes": {
    "Unsafe Response Rate": "The frequency with which a model generates harmful or inappropriate outputs.",
    "Over-refusal": "The tendency of a model to decline to provide information or assistance unnecessarily, potentially hindering user experience.",
    "Jailbreak Success": "Instances where users manage to manipulate a model into providing restricted or harmful information.",
    "Harmful Compliance": "When a model follows user instructions that lead to unsafe or unethical outcomes.",
    "Refusal Precision/Recall": "Metrics assessing the accuracy of a model's refusals, measuring how well it declines inappropriate requests."
  }
}
technical_feasibility: The study requires access to open-source GNN and LLM models for hidden state extraction and internal representation analysis. It also needs labeled datasets for training and evaluation, which should be sourced from scientific literature databases. Additionally, GPU resources will be necessary for model training and evaluation. If user trust is to be studied, a human-subject design is essential, along with measures for trust calibration. Missing resources include human participants for trust evaluation and potentially annotated datasets for interpretability assessments. A feasible adjustment would be to focus on output-level explanations using API models if open-source models are not accessible.
gap: Prior studies have demonstrated the integration of Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) and Large Language Models (LLMs) for knowledge extraction in specific domains like biomedical literature; however, they treat the empirical validation and interpretability of these models as secondary, leaving unclear whether the integration effectively enhances knowledge extraction across diverse scientific fields. This matters theoretically because understanding the scalability and applicability of these models can inform broader knowledge discovery processes; therefore, this study investigates the empirical performance and interpretability of GNNs integrated with LLMs for knowledge extraction from scientific literature across multiple domains.
question: How does the integration of Graph Neural Networks and Large Language Models improve the accuracy and interpretability of knowledge extraction from scientific literature compared to traditional machine learning models across multiple domains?
theoretical_mechanism: The independent variable in this study is the integration of Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) and Large Language Models (LLMs). The mediator is the enhanced representation features derived from GNN architectures, which improve the model's ability to capture complex relationships in scientific literature. The dependent variable is the accuracy and interpretability of knowledge extraction outcomes. The theoretical framework is grounded in knowledge discovery processes, where improved model performance is expected to lead to better system-level outcomes, such as reduced unsafe response rates and increased refusal accuracy, mediated by technical mechanisms like safety detection and steering. User-level outcomes, such as trust and satisfaction, are influenced by perceived transparency and calibrated trust, which are psychological mechanisms that mediate the relationship between model performance and user reliance. Assumptions requiring empirical validation include the effectiveness of GNN-LLM integration in diverse domains and the impact of representation features on interpretability and accuracy.
hypothesis: The integration of Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) with Large Language Models (LLMs) will significantly improve the accuracy of knowledge extraction from scientific literature compared to traditional machine learning models, mediated by enhanced representation features derived from GNN architectures.

Data will be sourced from diverse scientific literature databases, ensuring a robust representation of multiple domains, including biomedical and e-commerce literature. The evaluation will focus on accuracy, F1 score, and Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC) as primary metrics, alongside interpretability scores derived from probing and attribution methods. Baselines will include traditional machine learning models and existing GNN frameworks to establish a performance benchmark. Controls will involve fixed dataset splits and randomized hyperparameter tuning to mitigate overfitting. The study will also incorporate user trust assessments through surveys post-evaluation to gauge perceived transparency and trust calibration. This rigorous approach aims to validate the effectiveness of GNN-LLM integration in enhancing knowledge extraction accuracy and interpretability, while addressing potential confounds such as dataset variability and user feedback biases.

proposal: This research proposal aims to develop an innovative framework that integrates Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) with Large Language Models (LLMs) for large-scale knowledge discovery in scientific literature, specifically targeting biomedical and e-commerce domains. The novelty of this study lies in its empirical validation of GNN-LLM integration, addressing the significant gap in existing literature, which primarily focuses on isolated applications without robust empirical support for broader applicability. Prior work has inadequately addressed the interpretability of these models, often overlooking the complexities of knowledge extraction across diverse scientific fields. This study hypothesizes that enhanced representation features from GNN architectures will mediate improved accuracy and interpretability in knowledge extraction, thereby influencing user trust through perceived transparency. The theoretical framework posits that the integration will yield superior performance metrics—accuracy, F1 score, and Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC)—compared to traditional machine learning models, with operationalized constructs ensuring clarity in causal claims. Methodologically, the study will employ a comparative analysis against established baselines, including traditional models and existing GNN frameworks, with fixed dataset splits and randomized hyperparameter tuning to control for overfitting and variability in dataset quality. Evaluation metrics will encompass accuracy, F1 score, and interpretability assessed through probing and attribution methods. Furthermore, a comprehensive risk management strategy will address potential biases in user feedback and data sparsity, ensuring a rigorous approach to empirical validation. This research not only aims to advance theoretical understanding of knowledge extraction processes but also provides practical guidelines for deploying GNN-LLM models in real-world applications, thereby contributing to the fields of machine learning and knowledge discovery.

Core concepts include GNNs as neural networks designed for graph-structured data, LLMs for contextual text comprehension, and knowledge extraction as the process of deriving structured information from unstructured text. The study assumes access to open-source models and labeled datasets, leveraging GPU resources for training and evaluation. Positioned within the existing literature, this research addresses significant gaps in empirical validation and interpretability of GNN-LLM integration, which has predominantly focused on specific domains. The central research question investigates how this integration enhances accuracy and interpretability in knowledge extraction compared to traditional machine learning models. The theoretical mechanism posits that enhanced representation features from GNN architectures mediate improved outcomes in knowledge extraction accuracy and interpretability, influencing user trust through perceived transparency. The falsifiable hypothesis states that GNN-LLM integration will significantly outperform traditional models in knowledge extraction accuracy. Construct operationalization will measure model performance through accuracy, F1 score, and Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC), while interpretability will be assessed using probing and attribution methods. The methodology includes comparative analysis against traditional models and existing GNN frameworks, with fixed dataset splits and randomized hyperparameter tuning as controls. Expected contributions encompass theoretical advancements in knowledge extraction frameworks, technical innovations in GNN architecture, empirical insights into model performance, and practical guidelines for real-world applications. Novelty lies in addressing the scalability and interpretability of GNN-LLM integration across diverse scientific domains, while key limitations include potential overfitting, interpretability challenges, and biases in user feedback.

proposal_critique.revision_plan: Revise the gap stage to include a more critical analysis of existing literature and its limitations. Strengthen the theoretical mechanism by providing a detailed explanation of how GNN-LLM integration leads to improved outcomes. Clarify the operationalization of constructs and ensure that all measurement instruments are explicitly defined. Finally, enhance the coherence of the proposal by ensuring that all sections are tightly integrated and clearly communicate the contributions.

rubric_scores.level: 12-13: strong and clear research framing with minor conceptual weaknesses
rubric_scores.justification: The proposal articulates a clear research problem regarding the integration of GNNs and LLMs for knowledge extraction, but lacks specificity in defining how these constructs will be operationalized across diverse scientific domains. Major weaknesses: The operational definitions of key concepts such as 'knowledge extraction' and 'interpretability' are not sufficiently detailed, which weakens the clarity of the research boundaries. Next band requirements: To move into the next band, the proposal needs to provide explicit operational definitions for all key constructs and clarify the boundaries of the research problem.

rubric_scores.level: 12-13: mostly coherent with minor reasoning gaps
rubric_scores.justification: The proposal presents a logical flow from the problem statement to the hypothesis and methodology, but some assumptions regarding the effectiveness of GNN-LLM integration require more empirical support. Major weaknesses: The causal claims regarding the mediation effect of enhanced representation features are not fully justified with existing literature. Next band requirements: Strengthening the justification for causal claims with empirical evidence and ensuring that each component of the reasoning chain is explicitly linked would enhance coherence.

rubric_scores.level: 15-17: clear novelty with meaningful research differentiation
rubric_scores.justification: The proposal introduces a novel framework for integrating GNNs and LLMs, which is a meaningful advancement over existing methodologies, particularly in the context of empirical validation. Major weaknesses: While the proposal claims novelty, it does not sufficiently articulate how this integration uniquely contributes to theoretical understanding beyond existing literature. Next band requirements: To achieve a higher score, the proposal should explicitly delineate how the integration of GNNs and LLMs provides new theoretical insights or frameworks.

The methodology is generally sound, with a clear plan for comparative analysis and evaluation metrics; however, some aspects such as controls and potential confounds need further elaboration. Major weaknesses: The proposal lacks detailed descriptions of the controls and how confounding variables will be managed during the evaluation. Next band requirements: Incorporating more detailed descriptions of controls and a comprehensive risk management strategy would strengthen the methodological rigor.

rubric_scores.level: 12-13: strong literature grounding with good comparative analysis
rubric_scores.justification: The proposal engages with relevant literature and identifies gaps; however, it primarily summarizes existing work without sufficiently critiquing or situating its contributions within broader debates. Major weaknesses: The literature review lacks depth in comparing methodologies and does not adequately highlight unresolved tensions in the field. Next band requirements: To improve, the proposal should provide a more critical synthesis of the literature, identifying specific gaps and unresolved issues that the research addresses.

rubric_scores.level: 7-8: approaching PhD-level with some shallow areas
rubric_scores.justification: The proposal demonstrates a reasonable level of theoretical sophistication, but it lacks depth in discussing the mechanisms underlying the proposed integration. Major weaknesses: The theoretical framework does not sufficiently explain why the integration of GNNs and LLMs should work, nor does it discuss potential limitations or trade-offs. Next band requirements: Enhancing the theoretical discussion to include deeper insights into the mechanisms at play and addressing limitations would elevate the academic depth.

The proposal is generally well-structured and clear, but some sections could benefit from improved precision and conciseness. Major weaknesses: There are instances of repetitive phrasing and some technical jargon that may hinder readability for a broader audience. Next band requirements: Improving clarity and conciseness in writing, while ensuring that terminology is accessible, would enhance overall communication.

evaluation.comments: Total score: 78.0/100. Academic level: Master's-level. Major strengths: Clear identification of a relevant research problem.; Innovative integration of GNNs and LLMs.; Strong methodological framework with defined evaluation metrics. Major weaknesses: Insufficient operational definitions of key constructs.; Lack of empirical support for causal claims.; Limited critical engagement with existing literature. Required improvements for true PhD-level quality: Provide explicit operational definitions for all constructs.; Strengthen empirical justification for causal claims.; Enhance critical synthesis of literature to identify unresolved issues. Final verdict: The proposal demonstrates potential but lacks the rigor and depth expected of true PhD-level research maturity. Significant improvements are needed to meet the standards for a competitive PhD proposal.
